entries.meaning: Rāma departed, leaving that forest; the two lions among men possessed incomparable strength. Yet the Lord grieved like one separated from his beloved and spoke many tales and reflections: ‘Lakṣmaṇa, see the forest's beauty—whose mind would not be stirred by it? Every flock of birds and deer is with its mate, as if they were reproaching me. Herds of deer flee on seeing us, but the does tell them, “You have nothing to fear. Go enjoy yourselves; these men have come seeking the golden deer.” Elephants take their females along, as though teaching me. A scripture should be reconsidered repeatedly even when well pondered; a king should not be counted under one's control even when well served; and though a woman is kept within one's very heart, youth, scripture and sovereign are not under control. Look, brother, lovely spring has awakened fear in me, bereft of my beloved. Knowing me distraught by separation, weakened and utterly alone, Love has formed a hostile coalition with the forest, bees and birds. Seeing me, Love's messenger went to him with his brother and reported the matter; Love then seems to have encamped and halted his army here.’

Vast trees entwined with vines seemed to stretch many canopies. Plantains and palms were excellent standards and banners; no steadfast mind could look without enchantment. Trees flowering in many ways seemed archers equipped with countless arrows, while lovely trees here and there looked like separate warriors under shade. Calling cuckoos seemed intoxicated elephants; frogs and large birds recalled camels. Peacocks, cakoras, parrots, pigeons and swans were splendid horses, and flocks of partridges and quail the infantry—the army of Love defied description. Mountains and rocks were chariots, waterfalls kettledrums, and cātaka birds bards recounting virtues. Humming bees were drums and shawms, while the three kinds of breeze arrived as messengers. With this fourfold army Love roamed, challenging everyone. Those who see Love's army and remain steadfast are renowned in the world. Its one supreme strength is woman; only the great warrior who escapes her power prevails. Brother, desire, anger and greed are three exceedingly powerful villains: within an instant they agitate even the mind of a sage who is an abode of realization. Greed's forces are desire and hypocrisy, desire's force is woman alone, and anger's force is harsh speech, so eminent sages say after reflection.

Rāma, beyond the guṇas and master of all moving and unmoving existence, knows every heart, Umā. He displayed the helplessness of the lustful and strengthened detachment in the minds of the steadfast. By Rāma's grace anger, desire, greed, pride and māyā all fall away. The person toward whom that supreme actor is favourable is not deluded by the magic show. Umā, I tell you my own experience: Hari's worship alone is real; the whole world is a dream. The Lord then went to the shore of the lovely, deep lake named Pampā. Its water was pure like a saint's heart and four charming bathing-ghats enclosed it. Various deer drank water here and there as crowds of petitioners gather at a generous person's home. Lotus leaves hid the water so completely that its current and mystery could not be perceived, just as Brahman without attributes is not seen when veiled by māyā. All the fish were happy in one and the same exceedingly deep water, as the days of those established in dharma pass joined with happiness.

Lotuses bloomed in many colours and numerous bees hummed sweetly and loudly. Waterfowl and graceful swans called as if praising the Lord; gatherings of ruddy geese, cranes and other birds made a sight beyond description. The beautiful birds' delightful voices seemed to call passing travellers. Near the lake stood sages' dwellings, and charming forest trees spread in every direction: campaka, bakula, kadamba, tamāla, rose, jackfruit, palāśa and mango. Many trees bore new leaves and flowers while ranks of bees made music. A cool, gentle, naturally fragrant and delightful breeze blew constantly. Cuckoos sounded ‘kuhū, kuhū’; hearing their sweet call, even sages were drawn from meditation. Laden with fruit, all the trees bent close to the ground, like benevolent people who grow humble after attaining excellent prosperity.

Seeing the exceedingly lovely lake, Rāma bathed and received supreme joy. He saw the shade of an excellent beautiful tree and sat beneath it with Lakṣmaṇa. All the gods and sages came there, offered praise and returned to their abodes. The compassionate Lord sat completely content, speaking delightful accounts to his younger brother. Seeing the Lord suffering separation, Nārada became deeply concerned: ‘By accepting my curse, Rāma bears many heavy sorrows. I should go and behold him in this state; such an opportunity will not arise again.’ Taking his vīṇā, Nārada went where the Lord sat at ease, singing Rāma's deeds in a gentle voice and describing them lovingly in many ways. As Nārada prostrated, Rāma raised him, repeatedly embraced him, welcomed him and seated him nearby; Lakṣmaṇa respectfully washed his feet. After making many requests and recognizing the Lord's inward pleasure, Nārada joined his lotus hands and spoke.

Nārada said, ‘Hear me, naturally generous Rāma: beautiful, unfathomable yet accessible, giver of excellent gifts. Give me one boon I ask, Master, though you know the heart.’ Rāma replied, ‘Sage, you know my nature: do I ever hide anything from a servant? What thing can be so dear to me that you, eminent sage, cannot ask it? Nothing of mine is withheld from a servant—never abandon this trust through confusion.’ Nārada joyfully replied, ‘Then I venture to ask this boon. Though the Lord has countless names and the Vedas say each is greater than the other, may “Rāma” be greater than all the names, Lord, a hunter who destroys whole flocks of the birds of sin. May devotion to you be the full-moon night, and may that Rāma-name be its moon; may the other stainless names be constellations dwelling in devotees' heart-sky.’ The compassionate Rāma told the sage, ‘So be it.’ Nārada's heart overflowed with joy and he bowed his head at the Lord's feet.
